target.title: fix(auth): decouple plugin synthetic-auth from profile fallback for gateway attempts (#110103)
target.body:
Closes #110103

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where anthropic-vertex users whose only credential is Google ADC (Application Default Credentials) hit "No API key found" on gateway-routed model calls, even though the same synthetic ADC auth resolves under `--local` and the plugin itself confirms it works.

## Why This Change Was Made

A gateway direct-attempt sets `allowAuthProfileFallback: false` so an unrelated stored-profile store cannot replace or pre-reject the immutable env/config source. `resolveApiKeyForProvider` was gating the provider plugin synthetic-auth hook on that same flag (`allowPluginSyntheticAuth: params.allowAuthProfileFallback !== false`), so turning off profile fallback also silenced the plugin hook and the gateway path failed for ADC-only providers.

This adds a distinct `allowPluginSyntheticAuth` flag on `resolveApiKeyForProvider` and `getApiKeyForModel`. It defaults to the previous coupled value so existing callers are unchanged, and the two gateway direct-attempt seams (`runtime-plan/resolve-auth` and the embedded-agent-runner `auth-controller`) pass it `true`. Stored-profile discovery stays gated by `allowAuthProfileFallback`, so the prepared-attempt isolation invariant is preserved: enabling plugin synthetic-auth does not re-open the profile store.

## User Impact

anthropic-vertex and other GCP-ADC-only providers now authenticate over the gateway route the same way they already do under `--local`. No behavior change for any provider that resolves through a stored profile or an env/config key.

## Evidence

Two regression tests added in `src/agents/model-auth.test.ts`:
- a gateway-isolated attempt (`allowAuthProfileFallback: false`) now resolves plugin synthetic auth
- stored-profile isolation still holds: a stored api-key profile stays unresolved when profile fallback is off, even with `allowPluginSyntheticAuth: true`

Local run of the full model-auth suite (vitest 4.1.10, Node 24 on Windows):

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  162 passed (162)
```

## AI disclosure

This change was written with Claude (Opus 4.8). I reviewed the diff, ran the tests locally, and take responsibility for the contents.

## Follow-up (2026-07-19)

### CI
`checks-node-compact-large-4` was failing because `src/agents/btw.test.ts` mocked `./model-auth.js` without `providerHasPluginSyntheticAuthHook`. Fixed in `a23f36a881` by adding `providerHasPluginSyntheticAuthHook: () => false` to that mock.

Local re-run after the mock fix (Node 24, Windows):

``
 Test Files  8 passed (8)
      Tests  334 passed (334)
``

Files covered: `btw.test.ts`, `model-auth.test.ts`, `resolve-auth.test.ts`, `auth-controller.test.ts`.

The earlier `upload-store.test.ts` lease flake on `checks-node-compact-large-3` is outside this PR's diff (auth resolver only). Watching CI on the new head.

### ADC-only gateway proof (still blocked on this machine)
ClawSweeper asked for a redacted after-fix gateway run with ADC-only anthropic-vertex credentials. This workstation has no Application Default Credentials configured (`gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` reports credentials not found; `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` unset). I will not fabricate gateway logs.

Once ADC is available on a machine that can run gateway inference, I will post redacted terminal/gateway output showing:
1. ADC-only provider authenticates on the gateway path
2. stored-profile fallback remains disabled
